text:
alex: Quick help — node app started returning 401s only when reading API_KEY from .env, but curl with the same key works. Anyone seen this?

maria: Did you check the header that's actually sent? often it's a quoting issue from how env is set

alex: I printed process.env.API_KEY and it shows 'sk_live_abc123' (with single quotes) — i copied from some docs and stuck it in .env like API_KEY='sk_live_abc123'

kai: yup that's it. dotenv doesn't strip surrounding quotes. Your basic auth should be "Basic " + Buffer.from(apiKey + ':').toString('base64'). If apiKey includes quotes those get encoded too.

alex: ahhh. my header looked like: Authorization: Basic J3N... (starts with J3 = base64 of '\'') — no wonder :facepalm:

maria: two easy fixes: remove quotes in .env (API_KEY=sk_live_abc123) or sanitize in code: const key = process.env.API_KEY?.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '');

kai: also double-check you include the colon. Common bug: Buffer.from(apiKey).toString('base64') vs Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:`).toString('base64') — server expects username:password even if password empty.

alex: repro steps I used: node script prints header, curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "sk_live_abc123:" | base64)" https://api.example.com/status works; curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "'sk_live_abc123'" | base64)" https://api.example.com/status returns 401

devbot: quick tip: if running in docker-compose, avoid "API_KEY='...'" in the yml, use either:
  environment:
    - API_KEY=sk_live_abc123
  or an env_file with plain values. Docker may include the quotes otherwise.

maria: optional: add a small sanity check at startup that logs a redacted value if it has quotes or whitespace and exit with an instructive error. helps catch these in CI :eyes:

alex: thanks all — fixed by trimming quotes and adding a small check. will update README for onboarding. :thumbsup:
